# Independent adversarial audit of the nine-fourths profile obstruction

Status: proved statements about an abstract numerical profile system. No tensor character with the extremal profile is constructed, and no lower bound on matrix multiplication is claimed. The released manuscript's other lemmas are not certified by this audit.

Source: OpenAI, *An Upper Bound of 9/4 for the Matrix Multiplication Exponent*, 2 October 2026, Sections 2–5, specifically Definition 2.1, equations (2.3), (2.4), (4.4), (4.5), Lemmas 4.1, 4.2 and 5.1. Protocol pin: `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`. Primary URL: https://github.com/openai/math/blob/adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a/preprints/Matrix-Multiplication-Nine-Fourths-October-2-2026/paper.pdf . Full local text inspected: `work/agents/complexity_algebra/sources/mm9_4.txt`.

## Verdict and necessary corrections

The extremal profile in `work/agents/complexity_algebra/MM_PROFILE_BARRIER.md` satisfies every explicitly required numerical profile axiom, at `t=3/4`, over all positive integer arguments. It also satisfies the natural zero-axis extension and the additional boundary concavity inequality this extension permits.

Two corrections are needed in that note:

1. “No t<3/4 upper envelope can hold” has the inequality reversed. No `t>3/4` envelope holds globally on this profile. Every positive `t<=3/4` envelope does hold, because `1/t>=4/3`.
2. The cleared-denominator difference in `(1+1/(3j))^3 <= (3j+2)/(3j-1)` is `6j+1`, not `9j+1`. It remains strictly positive.

The obstruction has an exact strengthening: this profile is the **pointwise minimum** of the complete normalized, positive, symmetric, separately discrete-concave, shifted-tripling profile class. Thus the numerical system admits maximal feasible `t=3/4` exactly, not only a matching asymptotic exponent.

## Exact system extracted from the source
